title: Couples, babies and big news
subtitle: J'ai une grande nouvelle : je vais avoir un bébé !
summary: Announce and react to big family news - a baby, a wedding, maternity leave - and talk about couples and childcare.

lesson.heading: Une grande nouvelle !
lesson.text: Adrienne tells her friend Émilie she is expecting a baby. Big news is announced with **j'ai une grande nouvelle** and plans are told with **aller + infinitive** (*je vais avoir* - I'm going to have). Friends react with surprise and ask when and where.

examples.text: *Adrienne :* **J'ai une grande nouvelle** : je vais avoir un bébé !
examples.note: I have some big news: I'm going to have a baby!
Really? Are you happy?
Oh yes! I'm delighted!

examples.text: Mes parents vont être **fous de joie** !
examples.note: My parents are going to be wild with joy!
And when is it due?

lesson.heading: Key expressions
lesson.text: Short phrases for reacting to news and making plans. **Tu plaisantes ?!** (*Vous plaisantez ?!*) shows strong surprise or irritation. **Se débrouiller** and **s'arranger** both mean to manage, to find a practical solution.

examples.note: No idea! (= I don't know at all)
You're joking?!

examples.text: **Ça va être** super ! / **Ça va être** difficile.
examples.note: It's going to be great! / It's going to be hard.
We'll manage. / We'll sort something out.

examples.text: **Maintenant qu'**ils vont avoir un enfant, ils vont se marier ?
examples.note: Now that they're having a child, are they going to get married?
Who's going to look after the little one?

lesson.heading: Le couple
lesson.note: **Se marier (avec)** = to get married (to): *Adrienne va se marier avec Sébastien.* **Être marié(e)(s)** = to be married. The day itself is **le mariage**, and the bride wears **une robe de mariée**.

lesson.heading: Le bébé
lesson.text: A pregnant woman **est enceinte** or **attend un bébé**. She gives birth (**accouche**) in a clinic with a doctor and **la sage-femme** (the midwife). The due date is the expected day of **la naissance** (the birth).

examples.note: Adrienne is pregnant. She's expecting a baby.
The birth is due on 1 October.

examples.text: Le petit Eloy **est né** le 1er juillet.
examples.note: Little Eloy was born on 1 July.
She gives the baby a bottle.

examples.text: Il change **la couche** et met le bébé dans **le berceau**.
examples.note: He changes the nappy and puts the baby in the cradle.

examples.text: Le papa met l'enfant dans **une poussette**.
examples.note: The dad puts the child in a pushchair.

lesson.heading: Garder and les congés
lesson.text: **Garder** has two meanings: to keep something, and to look after someone. Time off work is **un congé**; going back to work is **reprendre** (= to start again).

examples.note: Are they going to keep the cat?
The grandparents are going to look after the children.

examples.text: Je vais être **en congé** du 4 au 7 juin.
examples.note: I'm going to be on leave from 4 to 7 June.

examples.text: Elle va être **en congé de maternité**.
examples.note: She's going to be on maternity leave.

examples.text: Je vais **reprendre** le travail le 8 juin.
examples.note: I'm going back to work on 8 June.

lesson.heading: Civilisation : le mariage et le Système D
lesson.text: In France the only legally valid wedding is **le mariage civil** at the town hall (**la mairie**); a religious ceremony can follow if the couple wishes. Many couples never marry - over half of babies are born to unmarried parents, and most women work. The French also pride themselves on **le Système D** (from *se débrouiller*): finding a quick, practical fix.

examples.text: On se marie d'abord **à la mairie**.
examples.note: You get married at the town hall first.
Babies are often born outside marriage.
I'll manage! / I'll sort it out!

lesson.text: Big events are announced on a card called **un faire-part** - *un faire-part de naissance* (birth) or *un faire-part de mariage* (wedding).

exercises.prompt: Match each French word to its meaning.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text:
*Émilie :* C'est vrai ? Tu es contente ?
*Adrienne :* Ah oui ! Je suis ravie ! Mon compagnon aussi... Et mes parents vont être fous de joie !

exercises.explanation: **Je suis ravie !** - she is delighted, and so is her partner.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text: *Corentin :* Ce n'est pas Sébastien qui va s'occuper du petit. Il ne va pas abandonner son travail !

exercises.prompt: What does Corentin think Sébastien is going to do?
options: Stop working to look after the baby.
exercises.explanation: *Il ne va pas abandonner son travail* - he isn't going to give up his job.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text:
*Adrienne :* Je vais être en congé de maternité du 31 août au 15 décembre.
*Étienne :* Vous allez reprendre le travail le 15 décembre ?
*Adrienne :* Non, je vais reprendre début janvier, après deux semaines de vacances.

exercises.prompt: When is Adrienne going back to work?
exercises.explanation: **Je vais reprendre début janvier** - after her leave and two weeks of holiday.

context.label: From the dialogue
context.text:
*Mme Martinez :* Qui va garder le petit ?
*M. Martinez :* Ils vont se débrouiller, ma chérie, parce que c'est nous qui allons garder le petit !

exercises.statement: Les grands-parents vont garder le bébé.
exercises.explanation: **C'est nous qui allons garder le petit** - Mr and Mrs Martinez, the grandparents, will look after the baby.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

pairs.right: demain, c'est la naissance du bébé.

pairs.left: Elle porte une robe de mariée, donc...
Les grands-parents vont garder les enfants, donc...
Élodie est la petite amie de Pablo, donc...
Sabrina va être en congé de maternité, donc...

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you a question and you don't know the answer at all. What do you say?
Choose the right word: Les grands-parents vont ___ les enfants. (= look after)
exercises.explanation: **Garder** means to look after someone; *conserver* is only for keeping things.

exercises.prompt: Elle attend un bébé, elle est ___.
Sort the words: do they belong to a wedding or to a new baby?

exercises.statement: En France, le mariage religieux se passe avant le mariage civil.
exercises.explanation: The civil wedding at **la mairie** comes first - it is the only legally valid one. A religious ceremony can follow.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence: "I'm going back to work at the beginning of January."
exercises.answer: Je vais reprendre le travail début janvier.
exercises.explanation: **aller + infinitive**: *je vais reprendre* - I'm going to start again.
